newsitem.title: INDIA: Funeral of Indian riot dead ends peacefully.
newsitem.headline: Funeral of Indian riot dead ends peacefully.

text.p: India's commercial capital was tense on Sunday after a day's strike but returning to normal as the funeral of 10 people killed in a riot ended peacefully, police said.
"The funeral has gone off peacefully," a police spokesman told Reuters. "But there is still some tension and we cannot rule out the possibility of trouble."

Police said about 10,000 people turned out for the funeral march for 10 people killed on Friday when police fired on a rioting crowd in the northeastern suburb of Ghatkopar, 15 km (9 miles) from the city centre.
The riot had erupted after a garland of shoes was placed on the statue of a revered leader of the lower social classes.

Angry mobs forced shops and businesses in Bombay to shut down in protest on Saturday. Protesters, reacting to what they said was a serious insult, blocked roads and railway tracks and threw stones at vehicles defying the protest strike.
Life in the bustling metropolis of 13 million people ground to a halt.

The suburban trains which form Bombay's lifeline were stopped after the crowds threw stones at them. Buses and private vehicles were badly damaged. The agitation also threw airline schedules out of gear.
On Sunday, transport services paralysed by the strike had returned to normal, officials said. Shops and markets opened for people to stock up on essential commodities.
Mourners sporadically threw stones at the paramilitary troops in riot gear lined up along the route of the funeral march, witnesses said.
"I saw at least 30 minutes of hectic stone-throwing," said a local resident. "The police beat up one or two people."
The protestors chanted slogans against the Hindu nationalist coalition government of Chief Minister Manohar Joshi and Home Minister Gopinath Munde.

At one point they turned on their own leaders, and beat up Ramdas Athavale, chief of the Republican Party of India, amid shouts that he was only interested in making political capital out of the incident.

Police said the riots and strike were a protest against the desecration of the statue of Bhimrao Ambedkar, a lawyer who helped draft India's constitution and was a dynamic leader of India's lower castes.
Police dispersed some protesters who tried to erect road blocks at Akola, about 500 km (313 miles) northeast of Bombay.
"Police were able to disperse the crowd without force," the spokesman said.
Opposition parties who called Saturday's strike in the city have called another one on Monday in the rest of the western state of Maharashtra, where Bombay is located.
But Bombay, where one person was killed in police firing on Saturday, would be exempted from Monday's strike, police said.
The Maharashtra government has ordered a judicial probe into the cause of the shooting.
